messages:
Ravi (PM): Heads-up: multiple enterprise accounts asking for an upgrade flow that keeps their external footprint identical. They also want smaller airgap bundles that don't require full-image swaps. Need to sketch acceptance criteria and a field runbook.
Tess (Eng): We can split the runtime into a core control plane and swappable workers. If worker binaries can be updated independently and we keep the same service IPs, customers won't see external changes. Means we need strict wire compatibility and handshake checks.
Omar (Infra): Wire compatibility is doable. We should add a compatibility matrix: protocol versions, admin ports, and cert expectations. Also suggest signing the delta bundles so offline installs can validate authenticity.
Priya (Field): From customers: they prefer "non-invasive" by default. Any step that touches route tables or public IP allocations is a blocker. They want a CLI preflight that outputs a single PASS/FAIL and a short human-readable remediation list.
Chris (SRE): Operational notes: provide a dry-run that simulates DB migrations (no writes) and a verification probe that runs smoke checks post-migrate. Also maintain a snapshot of pre-upgrade state (configs + routing) so rollback is deterministic.
Tess (Eng): Proposal for delta format: a signed manifest.json + patch.tar + migrations/ directory. manifest includes: version, component list, reverse-migration pointer, sha256s. CLI commands:
```
redwood-delta verify manifest.json
redwood-delta plan manifest.json --out plan.json
redwood-delta apply manifest.json --shadow (simulate)
```
Ravi (PM): Good. For product we need two customer-visible knobs: `preserve-external-ips=true|false` and `apply-mode={shadow,plan,apply}`. Defaults should be preserve-external-ips=true and apply-mode=plan. Document estimated window for each mode.
Omar (Infra): For preserve-external-ips we must document which IPs are guaranteed: LB VIPs and NAT egress ranges only. Pod IPs are ephemeral and cannot be preserved without heavy orchestration. Call that out in the docs.
Priya (Field): Add a short checklist NetOps can run: current VIPs, firewall rules to open, SSH bastion access, pre-approval from security. Make it one page. We can template it in the Console 'upgrade assistance' panel.
Chris (SRE): Rollback design: store the applied migration id in control DB and keep previous bundle cached for 72h. If health checks fail within a window, auto-initiate rollback to previous bundle unless `--manual-rollback` is set. Emit clear alerts with runbook link.
Ravi (PM): Prioritization: MVP (by EOW sprint) = signed delta spec + CLI verify/plan + documentation stub + field checklist. Stretch goals (next quarter) = console UI for preview, automatic canary on subset of tenants, network-shadow lab utility.
Tess (Eng): Dev tasks: manifest schema + validator, patch apply library with reversible operations, migration runner that supports dry-run and resume. I'll open a tech spike for reversible migrations.
Omar (Infra): We should add a network-preserve preflight that outputs a minimal JSON report for programmatic gating. Example: `{
  "vip_ok": true,
  "egress_conflicts": []
}`.
Priya (Field): I'll draft the one-page NetOps template and collect two customer contacts to pilot the flow. Also suggested we include an explicit customer-approval step in the CLI for production installs.
deploy-bot: Created ticket PRD-1202 "Signed delta bundles + IP-preserve upgrade path" (owner: Ravi).
Chris (SRE): One more: telemetry. Emit an anonymous upgrade-event (success/failure/duration) when allowed by customer opt-in. That helps us tune default SLOs.
Ravi (PM): Agreed. Action items: Tess -> manifest+validator PR by Thu. Omar -> preflight report prototype by Thu. Priya -> runbook draft and pilot list by Mon. Chris -> rollback alert playbook by Fri. We'll reconvene next Tue 30m to lock criteria. Thanks! :rocket:
